{{Short description|American chemist (1938–2024)}}
'''Eugene S. (E. S.) Stevens''' (born Eugene S. Pysh; 29 December 1938 – 16 December 2024) was a Professor of [[Physical Chemistry]] at [[Binghamton University]]. He was best known for his research in [[biodegradable plastic]]s.<ref name=Stevens>[http://chemiris.chem.binghamton.edu/STEVENS/stevens.html "Eugene S. Stevens: Bioplastics, Biopolymers and Renewable Materials Research"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402132003/http://chemiris.chem.binghamton.edu/STEVENS/stevens.html |date=2015-04-02 }} Binghamton University. Jan. 8, 2013</ref> He was a quoted expert in articles published in the [[The New York Times|New York Times]], [[Bloomberg Businessweek]], and the [[International Herald Tribune]].<ref name=Gies /><ref name=Kharif>Kharif, Olga [https://www.bloomberg.com/bw/stories/2005-03-02/from-nasty-bacteria-to-eco-friendly-bugs “From Nasty Bacteria to Eco-friendly Bugs”] Bloomberg BusinessWeek. March 2, 2005.</ref><ref name=Gies2>{{cite news |last=Gies |first=Erica |title=Beyond labels: Identifying the value of bioplastics |work=International Herald Tribune |date=July 7, 2008 |url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-153990991.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402112812/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1P1-153990991.html |archive-date=April 2, 2015 |via=[[HighBeam Research]] |url-access=subscription |url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Education==
Stevens received a Bachelor of Science degree in [[Chemistry]] from [[Yale University]] and his doctorate in Chemistry from the [[University of Chicago]]. Funded by a [[National Science Foundation]] Fellowship, he completed his postdoctoral work at [[Harvard University]].<ref name=Stevens/>
                   	
==Career==
Stevens conducted research in the area of biopolymers for over 30 years.<ref name= Gies>Gies, Erica [https://www.nytimes.com/2008/07/06/business/worldbusiness/06iht-rbogplast.sr.14263750.html?pagewanted=all&_r=0 "Bioplastics: The challenge of viability"] The New York Times, "Business." July 6, 2008.</ref>  He was the author of ‘’Green Plastics: An Introduction to the New Science of Biodegradable Plastics’’ (Princeton University Press, 2002), the first general audience book about the research and development of biodegradable plastics made from plants.<ref name=Green>[https://www.amazon.com/Green-Plastics-Introduction-Biodegradable-Plastics/dp/069104967X "Green Plastics: An Introduction to the New Science of Biodegradable Plastics"] Amazon Books. Accessed Feb. 15, 2015.</ref>  In 2012, the book inspired the invention of an edible [[LED lamp]].

Stevens' research involved the use of abundant, renewable [[biopolymer]] resources, specifically [[polysaccharide]]s—including [[starch]], [[cellulose]], and [[agar]]—for the production of degradable, [[Biodegradation|biodegradable]], and [[compost]]able products that [[Fossil fuel phase-out|conserve the use of fossil resources]] and divert waste plastics from landfills and incinerators.<ref name=Undergrad>[http://www.binghamton.edu/chemistry/undergraduate-program/undergraduate-research.html#stevens. “Guide to Undergraduate Research 2014-2015: Faculty Research Interests"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150328101714/http://www.binghamton.edu/chemistry/undergraduate-program/undergraduate-research.html#stevens. |date=2015-03-28 }} Binghamton University. Accessed Feb. 17, 2015.</ref>  His research was supported by grants from funders such as the National Science Foundation.<ref name=Award>[http://www.binghamton.edu/news/inside/news.html?issue=2003oct16&id=4 "Inside Binghamton University: Latest faculty research awards announced"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100531214622/http://www2.binghamton.edu/news/inside/news.html?issue=2003oct16&id=4 |date=2010-05-31 }} Binghamton University. Accessed Feb. 17, 2015.</ref>
  
His early career focused on studying the [[Conformational isomerism|conformational]] behavior of [[biomolecule]]s, a topic he explored through chiroptic methods.<ref name=Stevens2>Stevens. E.S. Green Plastics: An Introduction to the New Science of Biodegradable Plastics. Princeton University Press. Nov. 1, 2001</ref>

Stevens joined the faculty of Binghamton University in 1977.<ref name=Undergrad/>  In 2011, he received the Chancellor’s Award for Excellence in Faculty Service.<ref name=Service>[http://www.binghamton.edu/inside/index.php/inside/story/1957/chancellors-award-for-excellence-in-faculty-service1 "Chancellor’s Award for Excellence in Faculty Service"]. Binghamton University. Oct. 17, 2011</ref>

Stevens served as a speaker for the [[American Chemical Society]], reaching students and general audiences throughout the U.S.<ref name=Service/>

==Publications==

In addition to his book, Stevens wrote numerous articles that appeared in publications such as the [[Journal of Chemical Education]] and the Journal of Biobased Materials and Bioenergy.<ref name=Stevens />  He was also quoted in BusinessWeek regarding biotechnology advances.<ref name=List>[https://www.binghamton.edu/giving/news-events/newsletter/BUbelieveFall05.pdf "The 'A' List."] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130120091424/http://www2.binghamton.edu/giving/news-events/newsletter/BUbelieveFall05.pdf |date=2013-01-20 }} Believe! Binghamton University Foundation. Fall 2005</ref>

==Memberships==

Stevens was a member of the American Chemical Society and the [[ASTM International|American Society for Testing and Materials]].<ref name=Service/><ref name=Gies/>

==Death==

Stevens died 16 December 2024 in Binghamton, New York.<ref name=Death>[https://www.legacy.com/us/obituaries/name/eugene-stevens-obituary?id=57296409 "Eugene Stevens Obituary"]Legacy Obituaries. Retrieved: 17 January 2025</ref>
